limitations: Finite witnesses support separately reviewed universal proofs; neither a grid nor stationary-policy enumeration proves the whole behavioral-deviation theorem.
Synthetic laws imply model results, not observed causal effects or current legal collectibility. Adequate financing, enforcement and exit rights are stated assumptions.
The finite promise theorem excludes public lotteries, private saving and persistent hidden state. The relational result is not a general optimal-contract or renegotiation-proofness theorem.
